text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: P99 latency breach for service=redwood-runtime model=gpt-3.5-redwood-open region=us-west-2. p99=2.3s (SLO=1.0s). Streaming stalls observed. Paging oncall.

maria (oncall): ack. I’m digging into metrics now. Paging runtime team and SRE.

pagerduty: Paging kevin (runtime) via phone.

kevin (runtime): oncall here. Looking at traces and dashboards — p95 ~900ms, p99 2.2-2.6s. Seeing a big tail from streaming endpoints (chunk stalls / long decode times). No deploys in last 2h.

sam (sre): any node-level issues (OOMs, GC)?

kevin (runtime): no OOMs. Host CPU normal. What stands out: KV cache eviction rate spike starting 15:42 UTC and prefills dropped. Prefill hit ratio dropped 85% -> ~30% which means more decodes from scratch. Eviction storms correlate with tail latency.

julia (prod-eng): customers on streaming are reporting stalls and long response times. Which tenant groups affected?

kevin (runtime): appears cross-tenant but heavier for high-concurrency customers (dedicated pools + hosted). Suspect cache fragmentation + prefill vs decode imbalance.

maria (oncall): ok, mitigations we can try? temporary fallbacks, config tweaks, or capacity bump?

kevin (runtime): priority order: 1) reduce prefill pressure (disable prefill for streaming clients temporarily), 2) increase KV cache target size to reduce evictions, 3) throttle large concurrent streams / reduce max_batch_size for affected pools. I can try 1 & 2 quickly on a canary.

kevin (runtime): Running queries:
```
# kv eviction rate
rate(kv_cache_evictions_total{pool="us-west-2-prod"}[5m])
# prefill hit ratio
sum(kv_prefill_hits) / sum(kv_prefill_requests)
# p99 latency
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le))
```

kevin (runtime): command to update runtime config (canary):
```
curl -X POST "https://control-plane/api/v1/runtime/config" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"target": "canary(10%)", "changes": {"kv_cache.target_size_mb": 12288, "prefill.streaming.enabled": false}}'
```

maria (oncall): please note customer-facing channels. I'll draft a short status for Slack #general if this persists.

kevin (runtime): applied to canary 10% at 15:55 UTC. Watching metrics...

incident-bot: Deploy event recorded: runtime-config-update by kevin (canary=10%).

kevin (runtime): within 3 mins canary p99 -> 0.98s, prefill hit ratio on canary jumped back up to 78% for decode path (prefill disabled reduced prefill contention for streaming). Eviction rate on canary down ~70%.

sam (sre): good signal. any regressions on error rates / correctness?

kevin (runtime): no error rate increase; streaming chunk order/continuity verified on a couple test clients. Proceeding to ramp to 50%.

kevin (runtime): ramp to 50% at 16:02 UTC. Monitoring.

julia (prod-eng): beginning customer notification: "We are seeing elevated latency on streaming endpoints; mitigation in progress. No errors, just delays. Will update in 15 minutes."

kevin (runtime): ramped to 100% at 16:09 UTC. Global p99 drop to ~0.95s within 8 minutes. Prefill hit ratio global recovered to ~80%. Eviction rate back to baseline.

maria (oncall): great. Can you summarize impact window and what customers saw? I’ll include this in the incident description for postmortem.

kevin (runtime): impact window: 15:42 UTC -> 16:12 UTC (30 minutes) where p99 exceeded SLO. Customer-facing stall window concentrated in first 18 minutes. Approx ~3% of requests had latency >1s during window. No elevated 5xxs.

sam (sre): initial root-cause hypothesis: KV cache fragmentation + sudden prefill-request bursts led to aggressive eviction. Prefill logic tried to prime many keys concurrently, increased memory churn -> eviction storms -> more cold decodes -> tail latency amplification. Prefill vs decode imbalance (prefill dominates CPU/memory) appears to be the trigger.

julia (prod-eng): action items:
- Short-term: keep prefill.streaming.disabled until we deploy smoother prefill rate-limiting (owned by runtime).
- Mid-term: implement eviction smoothing and KV compaction.
- Long-term: adaptive prefill prioritization based on active sequences and memory pressure.

maria (oncall): I’m handing off to next oncall (kevin2) at 16:18 UTC. Summary: mitigated by disabling streaming prefill + increasing kv cache target size; p99 back under SLO; customer impact limited to latency, no errors.

kevin (runtime): creating follow-up tickets: INF-3245 (eviction smoothing), INF-3246 (adaptive prefill), INF-3247 (postmortem & monitoring alert tuning).

maria (oncall): severity set to sev2 (latency impacting but mitigated). Postmortem scheduled for tomorrow 10:00am PST.

julia (prod-eng): thumbs up on the ramp. Please confirm we have a rollback plan in case the config causes any regression (we do, control-plane can revert).

kevin (runtime): confirmed rollback steps in runbook.

maria (oncall): closing the incident thread as mitigated. Will attach timeline + graphs to the postmortem. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
